name: Crazy Diamond
description: You are given a permutation $$$p$$$ of integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$, where $$$n$$$ is an even number. Your goal is to sort the permutation. To do so, you can perform zero or more operations of the following type: take two indices $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$ such that $$$2 \cdot |i - j| \geq n$$$ and swap $$$p_i$$$ and $$$p_j$$$. There is no need to minimize the number of operations, however you should use no more than $$$5 \cdot n$$$ operations. One can show that it is always possible to do that.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \leq n \leq 3 \cdot 10^5$$$, $$$n$$$ is even) — the length of the permutation. The second line contains $$$n$$$ distinct integers $$$p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n$$$ ($$$1 \le p_i \le n$$$) — the given permutation.
output_specification: On the first line print $$$m$$$ ($$$0 \le m \le 5 \cdot n$$$) — the number of swaps to perform. Each of the following $$$m$$$ lines should contain integers $$$a_i, b_i$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i, b_i \le n$$$, $$$|a_i - b_i| \ge \frac{n}{2}$$$) — the indices that should be swapped in the corresponding swap. Note that there is no need to minimize the number of operations. We can show that an answer always exists.
